Kit

kit/comms — chat, pings, system lines

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Host routing and event deliveryAPI by taskWorked example (cavecrawl)Message ordering and limits

kit/comms sends text chat, positional pings/markers, and host-authored system lines such as "alice joined the cave". It uses the session's SES_APP messages on the reliable channel. The package supplies the packet format and routing; the game supplies the UI and system-line wording.

Chat operates at the session level and works with the cooperative lane, the simulation lane, or both. It does not participate in simulation ticks or prediction.

Odin
import kcomms "godot:kit/comms"

Host routing and event delivery#

All messages route through the host, which attaches the speaker identity and rebroadcasts them in host order. A client's own chat line is displayed when that broadcast returns, preserving the same ordering as other peers.

ksess.Host_Relay handles sender identity, source checks, echo policy, and replay to individual recipients. Comms sets echo = true, which delivers the host's broadcast back to its author. kit/comms adds encoding for two message kinds, a bounded log, and a shared event queue. comms_say writes the same payload on hosts and clients; the relay selects broadcast or upload without a caller-side is_host check.

The receiver delivers two kinds of events:

  • Lines land in a bounded log (LOG_MAX :: 64 lines, oldest evicted) that a UI repaints from; kit/ui's chat box does exactly this.
  • Markers (pings) are transient poll-once events, not log lines. The game turns them into world visuals.

The session admits only seated senders to the handler. Clients drop chat broadcasts received from any peer other than the host, preventing another client from submitting a broadcast with an invented speaker identity.

API by task#

Initialize: call once with the session, on the host or client, before or after session start:

Odin
comms_init :: proc(c: ^Comms, ses: ^ksess.Session, tag := COMMS_TAG)
comms_destroy :: proc(c: ^Comms)

COMMS_TAG is u8(0); pass another tag if the game claims 0 for itself (cavecrawl keeps comms on 0 and puts fire announcements on TAG_FIRE :: u8(1)). Destroy Comms before destroying the session, since teardown removes its route from the session.

Send player messages: hosts and clients use these procedures:

Odin
comms_say :: proc(c: ^Comms, text: string)                  // clipped to MAX_SAY (240 bytes)
comms_ping :: proc(c: ^Comms, kind: u8, pos: [3]f32)        // kind is game-defined; 2D leaves z zero

Send a system line: only the host may call this. The game supplies text such as "bob joined the cave":

Odin
comms_system :: proc(c: ^Comms, text: string)

System lines carry SYSTEM_LINE :: knet.Player_Id(0) as the speaker (real ids start at 1).

Replay history to a joiner: the host calls this on Ev_Player_Joined to send the log to that player:

Odin
comms_catchup :: proc(c: ^Comms, player: knet.Player_Id)

Consume: call this every frame:

Odin
comms_poll :: proc(c: ^Comms) -> (ev: Event, ok: bool)      // Event :: union { Ev_Line, Ev_Marker }
comms_lines :: proc(c: ^Comms) -> []Line                    // the log, oldest first
comms_line_name :: proc(c: ^Comms, line: Line) -> string    // "" for system lines

Ev_Line.text points into the log. Copy it if you keep it past a frame.

Worked example (cavecrawl)#

The frame loop polls events, repaints the chat box when a line arrives, and creates visuals for markers.

Odin
refresh_chat := false
for {
    cev, cok := kcomms.comms_poll(&self.comms)
    if !cok {break}
    switch e in cev {
    case kcomms.Ev_Line:
        refresh_chat = true
    case kcomms.Ev_Marker:
        gd.print_str(fmt.tprintf("CAVE_MARK player=%d kind=%d x=%.1f", u64(e.player), e.kind, e.pos.x))
    }
}
if refresh_chat {
    kui.chat_refresh(&self.chat, &self.comms)
}

On the host, comms_welcome sends history to a new joiner before broadcasting the join line. It skips history replay on rejoin:

Odin
case ksess.Ev_Player_Joined:
    if self.ses.is_host {
        if p, ok := ksess.session_player(&self.ses, e.id); ok {
            verb := e.rejoin ? "returned to" : "joined"
            kcomms.comms_welcome(&self.comms, e.id, e.rejoin, fmt.tprintf("%s %s the cave", p.name, verb))
        }
    }

Message ordering and limits#

  • Reserve a unique app tag. Comms messages use one tag inside the session's SES_APP framing. The game does not need a separate transport packet kind for chat. Other SES_APP users must choose different tags (see session.md).
  • Catchup before the join line. comms_welcome handles this ordering for you. The join line is broadcast to everyone, including the joiner. Replay the log first or the joiner sees their own arrival twice. Rejoins skip catchup (a same-session reconnect may still hold this run's log). Use comms_catchup/comms_system directly only when your join lifecycle differs.
  • Your own line does not echo locally (on a client). It lands when the host's broadcast comes back. Don't paint an optimistic local copy or you'll double it.
  • comms_system asserts is_host. System lines come from the authority; clients that want a system line must ask the host; ordinary player text uses comms_say.
  • Bytes, not runes: MAX_SAY is a 240-byte budget, clipped at a rune boundary (never mid-UTF-8). The host enforces the same limit again on receipt.
